chapter: Emmett Hardy, Bix and the Rhythm Kings
title: Louis Armstrong's claim about Hardy and the steamboat High Society contest
summary: He tells of a card from Louis after Hardy's death and of the boat contest where Louis called Hardy the king.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Now here's another thing. When he died, Bill, this is the God's truth, so help me. So help me. When he died, there was two things that his mother had. And if I'd only got them, you see, Louie disputed me about him and them and having a bucket contest on the boat.

He disputed that. He said the only old fae he ever played with was Bix. That's, that's, that's, that's not so. His mother had a card from Louie. And the card read, I, I read it with my, I saw it with my own eyes, Bill. The card read, now that the king is dead, I am the king. Signed, Louis Armstrong. That's what, it was a postcard. It wasn't a letter. Now from Bix, his mother had a whole letter of about a, about a full page letter saying how much he idolized Emmett, how much Emmett had done for him, both in Davenport and in Chicago. See, now if I could have got the hold of those two letters, I could have thrown that card right in Louie's face. And how that thing happened on the boat, you see, they had, wasn't the, wasn't the, the Sydney, I mean the, the president, or the capital, the boat preceding the, the capital. It was the Sydney, the one before, before the capital. And they used to give all day rides. They had music on there every night, not, not like, nah, weekends. They had music every night. And they used to give these all day rides. Well they'd either go down the river or go up the river, about 30, 40 miles, and they, and they'd dock the boat and then they'd have these picnics. You see, all day long, it was an all day affair, and they hired an extra band when they'd have these picnics. Two, in other words, they'd have continuous music. One band, like the door, one more, one, one band would play half an hour, the other band would play another half an hour. See, well Hardy, used to get that job. Every once in a while, that all day, those all day rides. And the, the, Louis was playing with faith. And they'd play on one side and they'd build a table.

temporary bandstand on the other side, where Harley would play, you see. And Harley only had seven men, and Fade had about ten or twelve men. So they got to playing, and the tune was high society. And Emmet was really blowing, and he was blowing so much so that they opened and instead of one, they had two spit valves on the horn. Two spit valves. He was blowing so hard he split both of them, his upper lip and his lower lip, too, from that all day, crying. And when he'd open up and let the water out of the horn, blood would go away, where he split his lips. But they got the gun on high society, and they must have played in high society for about twenty minutes, or half an hour. And when they got through, from the other bandstand, Louis made his bow and hollered all the way across the floor. Now, Tony Fougerite was there, too. Tony can tell you about that. He made his bow and hollered over across the floor. You is the king. Just like that, you know, I mean, recognizing Emmet, see. But then later on, when I got the story in downbeat, well then he denied of playing. But he might have said, might have thought it was a thing where he sat in with Emmet or something like that. It wasn't that. It wasn't a jam session. In other words, well, you know, why, because we did that forty years around. We used to sit in with him and record with him, nobody could see, you know. But I used to go back. They had a place back in tracks called The Entertainer. And they had a good band. I used to go back to sit in with him all the time. And they're in the same place, the Ritz, they had a color band, and I used to go sit in there with him.
